units: Targ. Ps. CXIX, 128 (Ms. Pa.).
Targ. Prov. XI, 6 תִּתְרוֹץ Ms. (ed. Pa.); a. e.

senses.gloss: to make straight; to arrange, lead. Ib. III, 6 יְתָרֵץ (some ed. תָּרֵיץ Part. Pe.).
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 33:27">Targ. Job XXXIII, 27</cite> Ms. (ed. Wil. <he>יִתְרִיץ</he>; h. text <cite ref="J00703"><he>יָשֹׁר</he></cite>!).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 39:33">Targ. Y. Ex. XXXIX, 33</cite>; a. e.—

<cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 29:34">Targ. II Chr. XXIX, 34</cite> <he>תָּרֵיצוּ</he> ed. Wil. (add.: <he>לבא</he>) they made their heart straight (ready; oth. ed. <he>תְּרִיצֵי לבא</he> were straight of heart; h. text <he>ישרי לב</he>).—

<cite ref="Gittin 4b:2">Gitt. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>רבה מְתָרֵץ לטעמיה ורבא מתרץ וכ׳</he> Rabbah settles (explains the differences of opinion in the Mishnah) in accordance with his principle (so that both disputants agree with his principle), and Raba in accordance with his.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 14b:14">B. Mets. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>לאו תָּרוּצֵי קא מְתָרְצַת תָּרֵיץ נמי בבעל חוב</he> must you not (in order to uphold the Boraitha) explain it (that it refers to robbers)? explain it just as well that it refers to a creditor.

<cite ref="Ketubot 35b:5">Keth. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>היכי מְתָרֵיץ לה</he> how will he harmonize the Mishnah (with his principle)? <cite ref="Shabbat 62a:15">Sabb. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>תָּרְצַת אשה וכ׳</he> you have explained the case satisfactorily with regard to woman, what have you to say concerning the case of man? <cite ref="Moed Katan 13b">M. Kat. 13ᵇ</cite>; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Berakhot 46b:7">Ber. 46ᵇ</cite> <he>מִתְרִיץ תָּרוּצֵי וכ׳</he> he (that reclines at a meal in front of another diner) would have to sit up in order to talk to him.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 170a:3">B. Bath. 170ᵃ</cite> <he>מתניתא לא מִיתָּרְצָא אלא כדמְתָרְצָהּ מר וכ׳</he> (not <he>כדמתרצא</he>) the Boraitha cannot be satisfactorily explained, except as you explained it, and this being so &c.; a. e.
